message.content:
You are sourcing ACTUAL current micro-SaaS acquisition listings for Hooman (Adobe eng manager; $25-150K capital; ~10-20 hrs/wk; wants a secondary income). He wants to see REAL options, not abstractions.

MARKETPLACE: Flippa (https://flippa.com/buy/monetization/saas). Note: most volume + most junk; exposes MRR/churn/age filters publicly.

Read the Buy Box first: Vertical B2B system-of-record / compliance / workflow SaaS in an unglamorous trade. Price $75-160K (sweet spot $80-120K). Net profit $2-5K/mo (realistic buys ~$1.5-2.5K/mo). >=18-24mo history. B2B recurring. Churn curve flattens. <20% customer concentration. Owner <10 hrs/wk. AI-safe: REJECT consumer apps, SEO/content sites, Chrome extensions, thin AI wrappers, single-platform (Shopify/WP/Stripe) add-ons the host can kill.
For full context, the playbook is at /home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/runs/buy_microsaas_PLAYBOOK.md.

Use WebFetch/WebSearch to browse this marketplace's SaaS listings (try the marketplace URL, its SaaS/B2B category pages, and Google queries like "site:flippa.combuy/monetization/saas SaaS" or "Flippa B2B SaaS for sale $100k"). Pull the ACTUAL listings currently visible — real titles, niches, asking prices, MRR/revenue, profit/SDE, multiples, age, tech stack. Prioritize ones near the Buy Box ($75-160K, B2B, recurring, boring vertical, AI-safe). Capture 5-12 real listings; for EACH, score buybox_fit and note exactly what data is gated behind a buyer account.

Be HONEST about access limits: if listings/prices are behind login, say so and capture whatever the public listing cards / category pages / Google cache DO show (many show niche + monthly profit + multiple + price publicly). Do NOT invent listings — only report what you actually find; if a field isn't visible, say "gated".

WRITE your findings to /home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/runs/buysaas_listings/flippa.md (use Write; create folders; include listing URLs where public). THEN return the structured schema.

content.content:
1	# 90-DAY ACQUISITION PLAYBOOK — Buy a Cash-Flowing Micro-SaaS
2	
3	**Owner**: Hooman Shariati (hshariati@adobe.com). **Written**: 2026-07-02 by Claude (Opus 4.8).
4	
5	**What this is**: The concrete, week-by-week execution plan for Hooman to buy ONE vertical-B2B
6	micro-SaaS. It operationalizes the research in `runs/buy_microsaas_research.md` and the prior
7	plan/validation (`runs/trackB/deep/buy_microsaas/02_execution_plan.md`, `03_plan_validation.md`).
8	Read those for the "why"; this is the "do."
9	
10	**The honest one-line verdict it implements (do not relitigate)**: This is a **capped-downside,
11	~13-22% gross cash-yield** capital deployment that nets **~$0-2.5K/mo of TRUE profit after his own
12	time** on the asset his budget can actually buy. It is NOT a $5-30K/mo passive-income machine. It
13	is worth doing only if (a) he has idle capital he can't deploy better, (b) he accepts owning a small
14	part-time job with real resale optionality, and (c) he clears **Gate 0** (below). If the true goal
15	is passive $5-30K/mo, one sub-$150K acquisition does not get there — do the ~$0 dry-run first and be
16	willing to walk with the capital intact.
17	
18	---
19	
20	## GATE 0 — DO THIS BEFORE SPENDING A DOLLAR OR AN HOUR (Day 0, free)
21	
22	**The single go/no-go question**: *Can Hooman honestly commit **15-20 hrs/wk (realistically 20-25 in
23	months 1-6, spiking on incidents) AND 8-12 hrs/wk indefinitely thereafter**, for at least 6 months,
24	without hurting CutLog?*
25	
26	- If CutLog is mid-crunch (a launch push, a 0→1 grind) → **DEFER the entire thing.** Do not split the
27	  building hours CutLog needs. This is a scheduling decision, not a deal decision, and deferring is
28	  the most defensible call per the validation.
29	- If YES, and he has a genuine calendar window → proceed to Day 1. Keep deal-flow (Days 1-50) running
30	  passively in the background; only pull the trigger (LOI/close) in a month CutLog has slack.
31	
32	**Also lock before Day 1**:
33	- **Pick 1-2 target verticals** he can underwrite credibly (see Ideal Target below). Being a focused,
34	  fast, confident buyer in a niche beats being a tourist across all of them — it wins the messy deals.
35	- **Accept the multiple reality**: he will pay **4-4.5x annual SDE** for anything not declining.
36	  3-3.5x = buying decline. Do not chase the 3x fantasy asset; it doesn't reach a slow solo buyer's inbox.
37	
38	---
39	
40	## THE IDEAL TARGET (the Buy Box — every line is a hard filter, not a preference)
41	
42	| Dimension | Hard filter |
43	|---|---|
44	| **Type** | Vertical B2B **system-of-record / compliance-recordkeeping / workflow tool** in an unglamorous trade. Moat = switching cost (customer's data/history lives in it) + domain trust. |
45	| **Revenue** | ≥18-24mo history; B2B; annual or sticky-monthly billing; **source-verified via read-only Stripe + bank** (never screenshots). |
46	| **Net (SDE)** | **$2-4K/mo trailing** — but underwrite knowing a fair multiple puts realistic buys at the **$1.5-2.5K/mo** end within budget. |
47	| **Price** | **$80-120K all-cash** (leaves room for costs + a $10-15K reserve inside the $150K ceiling). Expect **4-4.5x annual** for non-declining. |
48	| **Churn** | Cohort retention curve **actually flattens in the raw Stripe export** (not masked by new-logo adds). Re-baseline the model to **~4.5%/mo**, not ≤3%. |
49	| **Concentration** | **<20%** of revenue from any single customer AND no single acquisition channel carrying the business. |
50	| **Owner load** | Current owner **<10 hrs/wk** (proves part-time operability). |
51	| **AI-safe / moat** | **REJECT** consumer apps, SEO/content sites, Chrome extensions, thin AI wrappers, single-platform add-ons (Shopify/WP/Stripe app the host can kill). The Microns "AI Resume Checker / AI Writing Assistant / AI Book Summaries" listings are the archetype to reject. |
52	
53	**Concrete niches (boring, sticky, AI-safe, underwritable by an infra engineer)**: field-service ops
54	for a narrow trade (fire-alarm/backflow inspection, pool-service routing, septic/grease-trap logs);
55	niche compliance & recordkeeping (OSHA/EPA logs, HACCP food-safety, calibration/maintenance logs,
56	permit tracking); specialty-trade quoting/POS/scheduling (sign shops, upholstery, monument shops,
57	gunsmith FFL logs, vet/med-lab specimen tracking); property/HOA/self-storage admin; trade-association
58	membership/CE tracking.
59	
60	**Reframe his edge (per validation WRONG-4)**: Hooman's engineering skill is **diligence alpha
61	(spotting traps others can't), NOT value-creation alpha.** Small B2B SaaS churns on relationships/
62	support/domain trust, not ugly code. Do not pay a premium expecting to rerate via a rewrite.
63	
64	---
65	
66	## DAYS 1-20 — SETUP + DEAL-FLOW ENGINE (≈$0 spent)
67	
68	**Goal**: a running, filtered pipeline and a reusable diligence toolkit, so Hooman is a fast buyer.
69	
70	### Week 1 (Days 1-7) — Accounts + saved searches
71	- Open **buyer accounts**: **Acquire.com** (highest volume in the $2-8K MRR SaaS band — shop here
72	  most), **Empire Flippers** (most vetted, priced higher), **Flippa** (most volume + most junk),
73	  **Microns.io** (curated micro-SaaS, on-band). Verify buyer status where required (EF/Acquire gate
74	  contact info behind verification).
75	- **Exact saved-search filters** (apply on every marketplace that supports them):
76	  - Category/type: **SaaS** (exclude content, ecommerce, agency, app, newsletter).
77	  - Price band: **$75K-$160K** (buy in the $80-120K sweet spot; upper edge catches negotiable deals).
78	  - Monthly net profit: **$2,000-$5,000** (Flippa/EF expose "net profit"; on Acquire filter by TTM
79	    profit / revenue and read the P&L).
80	  - Age/history: **≥18 months** ("established"/"18+ mo" filters where available).
81	  - Business model: **B2B**, subscription/recurring; on Flippa set **churn, LTV, AOV** filter columns
82	    visible so they can be read at a glance.
83	  - Exclude: AI-wrapper, Chrome extension, single-platform add-on, marketplace/two-sided.
84	- Set **email alerts** on each saved search so new inventory pushes to him (deal-flow runs passively).
85	
86	### Week 2 (Days 8-14) — Build the reusable diligence toolkit (his repeat-buyer moat)
87	- **Financial model spreadsheet**: trailing SDE, MRR trend, self-built cohort retention curve,
88	  gross logo churn, revenue vs one-time/services split, customer concentration, true hosting/ops cost,
89	  underwriting at 4.0-4.5x with **zero growth credit**.
90	- **Code/infra red-flag checklist**: single points of failure; secrets committed in repo; backup story
91	  (exists? tested?); dependency rot; scaling-cost cliff; the one undocumented cron/hack holding it
92	  together; clean IP chain (every contributor's IP assigned — FE calls missing IP-assignment a top
93	  red flag).
94	- **Standard read-only-access request template**: read-only **Stripe** login, **bank/PayPal** statements,
95	  **Google Analytics / Search Console**, **hosting console**, **repo**. (No live access = walk.)
96	- **Killer-questions call script**: why selling; owner hrs/wk; top-5 customers' % of revenue;
97	  acquisition channel mix; tech stack; who does support today; what breaks at 2x scale.
98	
99	### Week 3 (Days 15-20) — Start the review routine
100	- **Deal-flow routine (make it a habit, ~3-5 hrs/wk)**: review **20-30 listings/week** against the
101	  Buy Box. Reject fast and hard — **90%+ should die on the paper screen.** Log every rejection reason
102	  in the model (builds pattern memory + speeds future screens).
103	- By Day 20: a **shortlist of 5-8** that pass the paper screen (GATE 1 — paper screen, free).
104	
105	**Reality check on supply**: cheap SaaS is abundant; clean, sticky, fairly-priced sub-$150K B2B SaaS
106	is the true constraint, and the buy-side is crowded ($2B+ verified buyer funds on Acquire + cash-ready
107	micro-PE holdcos). Expect to review **50-90 listings** across these 20 days to net 5-8 real candidates.
108	
109	---
110	
111	## DAYS 20-50 — DILIGENCE FUNNEL: SCREEN → LOI → DEEP DILIGENCE (still ~$0)
112	
113	**Goal**: take the 5-8 shortlist down to 1-2 finalists via source-verification and the code/infra
114	audit — Hooman's edge — then submit an LOI on the one that clears.
115	
116	### Days 20-28 — Seller calls, narrow 5-8 → 3-5 (GATE 1 confirm)
117	- Sign NDAs; run the killer-questions call on each shortlisted deal. Reject on any Buy-Box miss.
118	- Shortlist to **3-5** worth requesting live access.
119	
120	### Days 28-42 — Source-verification on top 2-3 (GATE 2 — the #1 gate, free)
121	**Revenue source-verify (no live access = instant walk):**
122	- Get **read-only Stripe + bank/PayPal statements** and **three-way reconcile**:
123	  **bank deposits ↔ Stripe MRR ↔ the P&L they showed.** Screenshots are worthless.
124	- **Build the cohort retention curve yourself** from the raw Stripe export. Confirm MRR is flat/growing
125	  on a **revenue-retention** basis, not propped up by new-logo adds masking churn.
126	- Separate **recurring MRR from one-time/services**; flag lifetime/heavily-discounted annual plans and
127	  **unscheduled discount spikes** (classic dress-up tactics).
128	- **Concentration**: <20% from any one customer; check acquisition-channel concentration (single-channel,
129	  esp. price-competitive PPC vs funded rivals = red flag).
130	- **Traffic** (if any SEO/organic dependence): pull GA/Search Console read-only; check no single
131	  keyword/referrer carries the business.
132	
133	### Days 42-50 — Technical diligence (HIS EDGE) on the finalist (GATE 3 setup)
134	- Read the repo + map the infra. FE calls **poor code documentation "deal-killing"** — confirm the
135	  **clean IP chain** (every contributor assigned IP; no missing contractor assignments).
136	- Hunt for: single points of failure, secrets in repo, no/stale backups, dependency rot, a scaling-cost
137	  cliff, one undocumented hack holding it together. **Price the true hosting/ops cost** (sellers
138	  understate it).
139	- Decide **"messy-but-fixable" vs "messy-and-a-trap."** Identify the 1-2 self-serve net-lift levers
140	  (hosting rightsizing, dunning) — NOT a rewrite.
141	- **Underwrite on trailing SDE only, zero growth credit.** If it pencils at **4.0-4.5x** with a genuinely
142	  capped downside → proceed to offer (GATE 3 pass).
143	
144	**The eight deal-killer red flags (walk on any):**
145	1. Seller **refuses live read-only Stripe/bank** → instant walk.
146	2. **Declining** revenue/profit dressed as "stable" (cf. EF #94153: −37% rev / −50% profit YoY).
147	3. **Churn masked** by new-logo adds; cohort curve never flattens.
148	4. **>20% single-customer** (or single-channel) concentration.
149	5. **Thin/undocumented code, unclear IP ownership**, secrets in repo, no backups.
150	6. **Platform-dependent** (host can kill it) or **AI-wrapper commodity** (an LLM can clone it).
151	7. **Lifetime/one-time revenue** dressed as recurring; unscheduled discount spikes.
152	8. **Owner-as-the-product** with no SOPs and no willingness to do a real 60-90d transition.
153	
154	**If nothing clears by Day 50 → that is SUCCESS, not failure.** Keep alerts running, keep reviewing,
155	never force a deal to a deadline. Patience is the entire risk-management strategy.
156	
157	---
158	
159	## DAYS 50-75 — OFFER, DEAL STRUCTURE, AND CLOSE
160	
161	**Goal**: submit a structured LOI that caps the downside, pass confirmatory diligence in escrow, close.
162	
163	### Days 50-58 — LOI + negotiate structure
164	**Recommended structure (this is what makes "downside capped" actually TRUE):**
165	- **All-cash on the bulk + 10-30% held as a 6-12mo earnout / seller note** tied to **revenue
166	  retention** (protects against the melting-ice-cube), **through escrow**, plus **non-compete** and a
167	  **60-90d paid seller transition + SOP handover** written into the APA.
168	- **Multiple**: **4.0-4.5x annual SDE (≈48-54x monthly)** for a non-declining asset. Pay the low end,
169	  or push toward 3.5x, ONLY if the numbers genuinely show flat-fragile/turnaround — and then price the
170	  base case as decline, not flat.
171	- **Use the earnout as a RISK-SHIFTER you request, not a discount you celebrate.** A seller who
172	  *eagerly* offers financing/earnout may be signaling low confidence in their own trailing numbers
173	  (adverse selection). Budget mostly cash regardless.
174	- **AVOID SBA / personal-guarantee financing.** SBA 7(a) acquisition loans require a personal guarantee
175	  (often a lien on personal assets/home) — that **destroys the capped, cash-only downside that is this
176	  idea's entire point.** All-cash caps max loss at the price minus resale; an SBA-leveraged deal can
177	  lose *more than the cash in* via the PG.
178	
179	### Days 58-68 — Confirmatory diligence in escrow (GATE 4)
180	- Legal review of the asset-purchase agreement (budget a lawyer, see P&L). Lock the transition plan +
181	  SOP handover + non-compete + earnout terms in the contract.
182	- Re-verify metrics have not moved; any material discrepancy → **walk** (escrow protects the money).
183	
184	### Days 68-75 — Close
185	- Fund via **escrow**; document the earnout/note. **Migrate everything**: domains, Stripe, bank/payout,
186	  hosting/DNS, repo, email, support inbox, customer records. Keep a **$10-15K working-capital reserve**
187	  untouched (EF: "never spend money unless you're okay losing 100% of it" — hold reserves for a slump).
188	
189	---
190	
191	## DAYS 75-90 — TRANSITION, FIRST IMPROVEMENTS, DELEGATION SETUP
192	
193	**Goal**: do-no-harm absorption, then the self-serve net-lift moves (his edge), and set the honest
194	delegation posture.
195	
196	### Days 75-85 — Absorb (do no harm)
197	- **Shadow the seller** on support; read every open ticket and the last 90 days of resolved ones.
198	- **Change NOTHING** on pricing or product yet. The months 1-2 goal is **stop the churn / do no harm**,
199	  not grow. (At ~4.5%/mo churn, two do-nothing months can bleed ~9% of MRR — minimize, don't add to it.)
200	- Start writing **SOPs** for support and routine ops as he learns them (prerequisite for any later VA).
201	
202	### Days 85-90 — First operating improvements (the moves that resolve the delegation trap)
203	Instead of delegating a too-small asset, **engineer net up himself** — cheaper than a VA+dev and
204	exactly where his skills apply:
205	1. **Cut hosting/ops cost** (pure margin; his infra edge) — the safest first win.
206	2. **Recover involuntary churn via dunning / failed-card recovery** — a one-time **~3-8% MRR lift**
207	   (this touches only the ~0.8%/mo involuntary slice; it does NOT fix voluntary churn).
208	3. **Ship one AI/feature win himself** if the codebase is clean enough.
209	
210	### The delegation setup — WHO does WHAT at WHAT COST (spelled out with numbers)
211	| Task | Delegable? | Cost |
212	|---|---|---|
213	| Tier-1 support / onboarding / mundane ops | Yes, **after SOPs exist** (month 6+) | Offshore VA **$300-1,500/mo** (~$5-12/hr, 20-40 hr/mo → $300-800; heavier front-line → $800-1,500) |
214	| Routine bug fixes / small features / dep upgrades | Yes, to a contractor dev | **$800-3,000/mo** variable (~$40-100+/hr) |
215	| Infra/hosting rightsizing | Hooman once (his edge), then rare | ~$0 ongoing |
216	| **Technical/escalated support, churn saves, key-account fires** | **NO — stays with Hooman** | his 8-12 hrs/wk |
217	| **Roadmap, pricing, dev direction, code review** | **NO — stays with Hooman** | included above |
218	
219	**THE DELEGATION-AFFORDABILITY CHECK (the core math — memorize the numbers):**
220	- The asset he can **afford** ($80-120K → **~$1.5-2.5K/mo net** at a fair 4-4.5x) **cannot afford to be
221	  delegated**: a $1,000-2,500/mo VA+dev spend consumes most-to-all of the profit → he'd be paying to
222	  own a part-time job.
223	- The asset **worth** delegating (**$4K+/mo net**, leaving $1.5-2.5K after a ~$1.5-2.5K delegation spend)
224	  costs **~$190-215K at a fair multiple — over the $150K ceiling.**
225	- **Rule**: **Delegation (VA+dev) only pencils above ~$4K/mo net.** Below that, Hooman IS the operator
226	  at **8-12 hrs/wk indefinitely** (steady state; 20-25 in months 1-6). Delegate later by **growing into
227	  $4K/mo**, not by delegating a small asset into the red.
228	
229	---
230	
231	## THE HONEST BUDGET (within $25-150K)
232	
233	| Item | Cost |
234	|---|---|
235	| Purchase price (mostly cash; 10-30% as earnout/note through escrow) | **$80-120K** |
236	| Escrow fee (~0.5-1% of price) | $500-1,500 |
237	| Legal review of APA | $2-5K |
238	| Diligence tooling / paid data | ~$500 |
239	| **Working-capital reserve** (transition dip + surprises) | **$10-15K** |

## Access notes (what's public vs gated)

- The category page (`/buy/monetization/saas`) renders listings **client-side** — WebFetch on the
  raw HTML returns "No matches found" / template placeholders. The public data is reachable via
  Flippa's JSON API (`flippa.com/v3/listings?filter[property_type]=saas...`), which is how the cards
  below were pulled.
- **Publicly visible per listing (no login)**: title, niche, asking price, MRR, monthly net profit,
  profit/revenue multiple, age/established, B2B vs B2C, subscriber count, headline churn %, and a
  "verified / vetted / data-verified" badge (whether Stripe + Google Analytics are connected).
- **Gated behind a free account / NDA**: detailed financials (P&L, cohort data), full traffic
  analytics, seller notes, and tech-stack specifics. **Tech stack is almost never public** — shows as
  "not disclosed" on nearly every listing.
- **Verification caveat**: "verified" on Flippa = a Stripe/GA integration is connected, NOT a
  three-way bank↔Stripe↔P&L reconcile. Per the playbook, still do live read-only Stripe + bank
  yourself (Gate 2). Multiples shown on cards are often internally inconsistent (see AssistLayer).

---

## Best-fit candidates (near the Buy Box)

### 1. Cloud-based IMS / ISO Management System SaaS — STRONG-ish
- URL: https://flippa.com/11797351
- Price **$139,284** (reduced 20%) | ARR ~EUR 28,240 (~EUR 2,353/mo) | Profit **EUR ~1,154/mo** | ~4.8x rev / 6.7x profit

  certainly >20% per customer), 11% churn is high, profit ~$1.2K/mo is at the low end, price is at the
  top of the band for that profit. Worth a call but underwrite churn/concentration hard.

### 2. Automated NHS IT Business (zero-touch laptop provisioning) — PARTIAL
- URL: https://flippa.com/12530181
- Price **GBP 75,000 (~$101K)** | Rev GBP 2,475/mo | Profit **GBP 1,250/mo** | 5.0x | Age **2 years** (Jan 2024)
- B2B (GP surgeries, locum agencies, locum GPs) | **18 clients** | churn **5%** | **Vetted (Flippa-verified revenue)** | owner **~30 min/month**
- **Fit**: Boring vertical (healthcare IT ops), 2yr history, genuinely low owner load, fair 5x, on-band
  price, churn 5% ~ playbook's re-baselined ~4.5%. **Concerns**: 18 clients = concentration risk;
  "IT provisioning" leans services, verify how recurring the revenue really is vs one-time device
  setups. Not a pure system-of-record but sticky-adjacent. Reasonable paper-screen pass.

- URL: https://flippa.com/12279687
- Price **$109,287** (reduced 20%) | Rev ~CAD 3,989/mo | Profit **CAD ~1,616/mo** | 2.7x rev / 6.3x profit

  — confirm it's a workflow/records tool with a data moat, not a thin LLM wrapper. 6.3x profit is

  monthly (~5.7x annual-ish but the card math is muddy); MarTech tracking is somewhat commoditizable
  and platform/pixel-dependent (privacy/ad-platform changes can kill it). Marginal.

### 5. Cloud-based IMS (business software) — see #1 (same category, another listing)
- URL: https://flippa.com/11797351 (canonical above)

---

## In-band but likely REJECT (age/wrapper/model flags)

### AssistLayer — Profitable AI customer support SaaS — REJECT (age + AI-wrapper)
- URL: https://flippa.com/12873277
- Price **$110,000** (reduced 8%) | MRR **$18,419** | Profit **$10,436/mo** | 97% margin | ~10.5x monthly profit (card's "1.8x" is wrong)
- Age **7 months** | B2B | **82 paying orgs** | churn **1%** | GA-verified | solo founder
- **Reject reason**: 7mo history (< 18-24mo minimum) and it's an AI customer-support wrapper — exactly
  the "thin AI wrapper an LLM can clone" reject class. Strong numbers but fails two hard filters.

### White-Label AI Logistics Load Planning (SMART LP) — REJECT (age + white-label + AI)
- URL: https://flippa.com/12935336
- Price **$220K BIN / $150K start** | Profit **$7,525/mo** | Age **1 year** | Gemini-AI + 3D viz | churn 0% | financials gated
- **Reject reason**: 13mo age, "white-label non-exclusive license" (you're not buying the sole
  business — seller keeps reselling it), AI-optimization wrapper. Fails moat + history.

### Screenify — AI recruitment/interview SaaS — REJECT (AI-wrapper, tiny base)
- URL: https://flippa.com/12258905
- Price **$75,000** | MRR $3,605 | Profit **$1,487/mo** | 4.2x | Age **2 years** | B2B | **6 subscribers** | churn 0% | **Stripe + GA verified** | 142% YoY
- **Reject reason**: only 6 paying subscribers (massive concentration), and "AI interview screening"
  is a thin-wrapper category. Verified Stripe and fair 4.2x are nice, but 6 customers ≠ a business
  with a flattening cohort curve. Reject on concentration + AI-safety.

### Native Email App Built For Whop — REJECT (single-platform add-on)
- URL: https://flippa.com/12268124
- Price $112.5K | MRR $3.8K | Profit $3.1K/mo | ~36x monthly | Age 8mo | B2B
- **Reject reason**: built entirely on the Whop platform (host can kill it) + 8mo history. Classic
  single-platform-add-on reject.

### Credit Building AI Platform — REJECT (fintech/regulatory + age)
- URL: https://flippa.com/12514968
- Price $100K | MRR $11.3K | Profit $10.6K/mo | Age 9mo | B2B/B2C fintech
- **Reject reason**: 9mo history and consumer-fintech/credit (regulatory exposure); off-profile.

### AI Video Dubbing SaaS — REJECT (AI-wrapper media)
- URL: https://flippa.com/12212870
- Price $145K | MRR $4.3K | Profit $3.8K/mo | Age 3yr | ~38x monthly
- **Reject reason**: media/AI-generation wrapper, easily cloned; not a boring B2B system-of-record.

---

## Bottom line for the paper screen

Real inventory exists on-band, but the clean vertical-B2B system-of-record deals are scarce and the
ones that exist share the **low-subscriber-count / high-concentration** problem (9-18 customers is
typical at this price). The three worth a killer-questions call:
1. **IMS/ISO compliance SaaS** (#11797351) — best archetype, but verify 11% churn + 9-customer concentration.
2. **NHS IT provisioning** (#12530181) — Flippa-verified, ~30min/mo owner load, but confirm recurring vs one-time.
3. **Property-manager SaaS** (#12279687) — Stripe-verified, 2.9% churn, 5yr history; confirm it's a
   records/workflow tool, not an AI wrapper, and negotiate off 6.3x.

Everything with the eye-catching profit ($7-10K/mo at ~$100-150K) fails on **age (<18mo) or
AI-wrapper/platform-dependency** — the market prices those low precisely because buyers discount the
moat. That matches the playbook's supply reality: cheap SaaS is abundant; clean/sticky/fairly-priced
sub-$150K B2B SaaS is the true constraint.
